takeaways: A meaningful image needs a text alternative that does the same job as the image.
Decorative images are marked so assistive tech skips them.
Icon-only buttons need a name. Describe the action, not the picture: “Close”, not “X icon”.
Complex images such as charts need a short alternative plus a longer description nearby.
failures: Icon buttons with no accessible name
Alt text that says “image” or repeats the file name
check: For each image, ask: if it vanished, what would be lost? Write that down.
Mark every image as decorative or meaningful in the file.

quiz.question: A magnifying-glass icon button submits a search. What is the best text alternative?
quiz.why: Describe what the control does. The picture means nothing to someone who cannot see it.

spec: Annotate each image as decorative or meaningful.
Write the alt text yourself for meaningful images.
Give every icon-only control its accessible name.
review: Who wrote the alt text here: the designer, or nobody?
Which icons have no visible label, and what are they called?
What is the text equivalent of this chart?
tradeoff: Icon-only interfaces are compact and ambiguous for everyone. Where space allows, a visible label beats a hidden name.
system: Make the accessible name a required property on icon button and image components.
pitch: Alt text is content. If nobody owns it, it ships empty.
